entries.reason: not carried, and it is state the system sets rather than data a domain holds: NSFileProviderDomain.h:150 reads "If set, the domain is present, but disconnected from its extension", so the property answers a question about an extension, and on this release there is no extension to ask about. That was measured from this port and not assumed: NSFileProviderExtension and NSFileProviderReplicatedExtension are 0 entries of the 7187 class names of the armv7 shared cache of iOS 4.3, and the release cannot answer it either - NSFileProviderDomain and NSFileProviderManager are 0 entries of the same list - while the control reads of those same two caches come back, description and copy being 1 of the 113981 selectors of 6.1.3 and 1 of the 70062 of 4.3. The state is also the one member a domain never has on its own: the header says it "can be modified on an existing domain via the disconnectWithReason method on NSFileProviderManager", and the port carries that method answering the one error a release with no extension host gives, -2001 "The application cannot be used right now" (NSFileProviderManager.m:169 for the error and :185 for the method). So nothing would ever set the flag and nothing would ever clear it, and either value would be a claim about a system that does not exist here

entries.reason: not carried, because what the property promises is a change to a system and there is no system here to change: NSFileProviderDomain.h:184 says "Enabling a testing mode alters the behavior of the system and enables some APIs for that mode", and :191 adds that "A process must have the com.apple.developer.fileprovider.testing-mode entitlement in order to configure a domain with non-empty testing modes". A value this port would keep and hand back would answer YES to a question about an entitlement the process does not have and change nothing the caller could observe - which is the fiction this file was written to refuse, in the sentence at FileProvider11.m:26, "inventing behaviour the release cannot have is the whole risk in carrying a framework". entries.reason: not carried, because it names something the port has no counterpart of: NSFileProviderDomain.h:208 says "Identity of the backing store of the domain on the system" and :210 "This property only applies for extensions that implement NSFileProviderReplicatedExtension", and :214 goes on to say what the identity means - the system "has dropped its backing store and is building a new one", and the identity "is guaranteed to be stable for the lifetime of the NSFileProviderReplicatedExtension instance". There is no backing store here to identify and no replicator whose lifetime could make an identity stable: NSFileProviderReplicatedExtension is 0 entries of the 7187 class names of the armv7 shared cache of iOS 4.3, and the port carries no replicated extension of its own. The identity is also the system's to change - the same header names -[NSFileProviderManager reimportItemsBelowItemWithIdentifier:completionHandler:] as a way to force it - so a value a domain held would be an identity the port made up. Measured rather than assumed: backingStoreIdentity is in none of the 113981 selectors of 6.1.3 nor of the 70062 of 4.3, against the control reads description and copy at 1 of each
